data.body:
## Live migration complete — acceptance criteria verified

Two passes, 106 tickets total.

**Pass 1 (104 tickets):** 91 closed, 10 idea, 2 open, 1 in_progress.
**Pass 2 (2 tickets):** `ace2-f784-4b19-4f22` and `d6a0-743b-71f9-4a5a`, which pass 1
silently skipped — their headings carry a parenthetical qualifier
(`## Success Criteria (target state)`, `## Success Criteria (outcomes, not mechanisms)`)
and heading detection was exact-string-match. Fixed by matching the SC and AC headings by
anchored, case-insensitive prefix pattern with a word boundary, emitting the canonical
`## Acceptance Criteria` so a qualifier is dropped with the heading rather than demoted
into a checklist item.

**Final verification against the live store:**

| criterion | result |
|---|---|
| tickets still carrying a Success Criteria **heading** (any variant) | **0** |
| further migrations proposed (complete + idempotent) | **0** |
| migrated tickets below the AC floor (`_count_ac_items < 1`) | **0** of 106 |
| migrated tickets missing from the store | **0** |
| tickets mentioning the string in **prose** — correctly untouched | 8 |

The 8 prose mentions are this epic's own tickets discussing the migration, where the string
appears backticked mid-line rather than as a heading. Migrating those would corrupt their
prose, so a guard test pins that direction explicitly.

**Rollback.** Pre-run descriptions captured at
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-sc-migration-restore-2026-07-25.json` (104) and
`…-stragglers.json` (2). Every change went through `rebar.edit_ticket`, so each is an
auditable event and `rebar revert <id> <event-uuid>` is the second restore route. This
answers the plan review's 'no rollback path' advisory.

**Oracle.** 27/27 green (2 happy-path + 25 held-out). Both defects that reached the live
data were caught by verification against the real store *before* damage: the order-sensitivity
bug (which would have corrupted 97 of 104) by the dry-run, and the qualified-heading miss by
post-run verification. Each is now pinned by RED-first held-out cases.
